needs.what: a command to run, or something to import
needs.why: Nothing here is walked otherwise, and a run that walks nothing still finishes and still says nothing changed.
needs.fix: Add `process: { commands: [{ name: "help", run: "node bin/cli.js --help" }] }` to your settings, or `imports: [{ name: "the package entry", module: "index.js" }]`.
needs.unlocks: Everything a command does — what it printed, what it exited with, what it wrote to disk, what it reached for.

surfaces.name: servers and APIs
surfaces.summary: Mostly covered. Without a way to restore the same data twice, anything that depends on stored data cannot be compared fairly.

needs.what: a database snapshot that can be restored twice
needs.why: Both builds have to see identical data or every difference is really a data difference.
needs.fix: Install Docker, or point the settings at a dump file the tool may restore.
needs.unlocks: Anything on your server that depends on stored data — totals, lists, permissions — gets compared fairly instead of being left out.

surfaces.name: native Windows apps
surfaces.summary: Nothing to check: this project names no native Windows program in its settings. Most Windows products are Electron, and those are covered over their debug port from any machine.
surfaces.instead: A native Windows window can only be read from Windows itself, and no Windows desktop answers from here. If your Windows product is Electron — most are — it is already covered over its debug port and you need nothing. If it is genuinely native, this becomes possible the day an SSH host in your config reaches a Windows machine.

covers.short: Nothing is set up in this folder, so a check cannot run here at all and would cover nothing. Run `staysfixed init` first. Once it is set up, this machine can drive web apps and sites. It covers command-line tools and libraries and servers and APIs only partly — read the summary for each before treating a clean result as proof. It does NOT check Electron desktop apps, Android apps, iPhone apps, on the simulator, native Windows apps, native Mac apps and native Linux desktop apps at all, so a clean result says nothing whatever about those. There is nothing of those kinds in this repository — Electron desktop apps, Android apps, iPhone apps, on the simulator, native Windows apps, native Mac apps and native Linux desktop apps — so there is nothing here to check, and that is not a limit of this machine.
